candidates.exact_span: a.   Pollutant Table (2 or 3) appropriate for permittee's land app lication practices.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Table 2 (loading-rate limits) or Table 3 (concentration criteria) governs depends on which table is 'appropriate' for the permittee's land-application practices; a different table choice changes which numeric limits apply (A) and which pollutant reporting framework is required (B).

candidates.exact_span: b.   The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 1, Section I.C. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable monitoring frequency is determined by cross-reference to Element 1, Section I.C.; different readings of which subsection applies change which monitoring intervals were obligatory in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: c.   Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) results (Pass/Fail).
candidates.computation_change_reason: TCLP is a Pass/Fail criterion rather than a numeric concentration limit; interpretation affects whether a numeric compliance comparison is applicable (A), whether annual TCLP monitoring was required (B), and how absent or non-numeric TCLP results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: d.   The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 1 (defined as a monthly average) as well as the applicable pollutant concentration criteria (mg/K g) listed in Table 3 found in Element 1, Section III, or the applicable pollutant loading rate limit (kg/ha) listed in Table 2 above if it exceeds 90% of the limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This item ties reported Table 1 concentrations to either Table 3 concentration criteria or Table 2 loading-rate limits, introduces a 90% threshold for when Table 2 limits must be reported, and defines values as monthly averages; different interpretations of which limit type applies, whether the 90% condition is met, or what 'monthly average' means would change limit applicability (A), reporting/monitoring obligations (B), and how missing or threshold-conditional results are handled (C).

candidates.exact_span: e.   Level of pathogen reduction achieved (C lass A or Class B).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Class A versus Class B pathogen reduction affects which downstream permit conditions and limit sets apply (including Section III eligibility); a different classification changes both applicable numeric limits (A) and associated monitoring/reporting requirements (B).

candidates.exact_span: f.   Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.3.(a. or b.). Alternatives describe how the pathogen reduction requirements are met. If Class B sludge, include information on how site restrictions were met in the DMR comment section or attach a separate sheet to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which pathogen-reduction alternative applies and whether Class B site-restriction documentation is required depend on permittee-specific conditions; different interpretations change what monitoring/documentation was obligatory (B) and whether missing site-restriction evidence is a required-data gap or not applicable (C).

candidates.exact_span: k.   The certification statement listed in 503.17(a)(4)(i)(B) or 503.17(a)(5)(i)(B) whichever applies to the permittees sludge treatment activities shall be attached to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which of the two 503.17 certification provisions applies depends on the permittee's sludge treatment activities; a different applicability determination changes the required certification obligation (B) and whether absent certification is missing required evidence or not required (C).

candidates.exact_span: l.   When the amount of any pollutant applied to the land exceeds 90% of the cumulative pollutant loading rate for that pollutant, as described in Table 2, the permittee shall report the following information as an attachment to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 90% cumulative loading-rate threshold triggers additional reporting obligations and references Table 2 limits; different interpretations of when a pollutant amount 'exceeds 90%' of the cumulative loading rate change which limits are operative for comparison (A), which supplemental monitoring/reporting is required (B), and how to classify periods without the triggered attachment evidence (C).
